merger_name: Woodside – PetroChina’s interest in Browse unincorporated joint venture

merger_description:
Woodside Browse Pty. Ltd. (**Woodside Browse**) is a subsidiary of Woodside Energy Group Ltd (**Woodside**). Woodside is a global independent energy company listed on the ASX and the New York Stock Exchange. Woodside’s portfolio includes explorations, developments, and oil and gas projects, which include the production of liquefied natural gas (**LNG**), natural gas for domestic supply (domestic gas), oil, condensate, natural gas liquids (**NGLs**) and ammonia.

PetroChina International Investment (Australia) Pty Ltd is a subsidiary of PetroChina Company Limited (together, **PetroChina**). PetroChina is owned by the China National Petroleum Corporation (**CNPC**), which is owed by the Government of the People’s Republic of China. PetroChina engages in the exploration and development of oil and gas reserves, and the supply of oil and gas.

Woodside (including Woodside Browse) and PetroChina are both involved in the exploration and development of natural gas reserves and both currently hold participating interests in the Browse unincorporated joint venture (**Browse JV**). Woodside Browse is looking to acquire PetroChina’s 10.67% participating interest in the Browse JV (the **Acquisition**). Woodside Browse already holds a 30.60% participating interest in the Browse JV and Woodside Energy Ltd is the current operator for the Browse JV.

The Browse resource is an undeveloped conventional gas resource with potential production of LNG, condensate, NGLs and domestic gas, located off the west coast of Australia. The Browse JV is proposing to develop the Calliance, Brecknock and Torosa conventional natural gas fields located in the Browse Basin (**Browse Project**). The proposed concept includes two floating production storage and offloading facilities, and a pipeline connecting to existing infrastructure for the North West Shelf. Natural gas extracted from the Browse Basin will be processed at the Karratha Gas Plant in Western Australia into LNG for export and domestic gas.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the Acquisition does not result in the removal of a
competitor or substantial change to Woodside’s competitive
position as it is already a party to the Browse JV and the
Browse JV is not currently producing gas in WA
b. domestic gas supply and prices in WA are regulated by the
Western Australian Government
c. there are alternative producers and suppliers of LNG and
domestic gas to customers in WA.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
